Claiming game: with multiset $M$ of pieces, players alternately take any piece. First player's optimal value is $\operatorname{odd}(M)$ — the sum of odd-indexed pieces in decreasing order. This is a standard result. Let me verify Lemma 1.1.

Lemma 1.1: first player can guarantee $\operatorname{odd}(M)$, second player can guarantee $\operatorname{even}(M)$. Since these sum to total, value of the game is exactly $\operatorname{odd}(M)$.

First player's guarantee: take $p_1$; suppose second takes $p_j$, $j \ge 2$. Remainder $M' = M \setminus \{p_1, p_j\}$ with sorted order $p_2, \dots, p_{j-1}, p_{j+1}, \dots, p_m$. Odd-indexed elements of $M'$: indices in $M'$: position 1 is $p_2$, position 2 is $p_3$, ..., position $i-1$ is $p_i$ for $i \le j-1$; then position $j-1$ is $p_{j+1}$, i.e., position $i - 2$ is $p_i$ for $i \ge j+1$. So odd positions of $M'$: $p_i$ with $i-1$ odd, i.e., $i$ even, $i \le j-1$; and $p_i$ with $i-2$ odd, i.e., $i$ odd, $i \ge j+1$.

So $\operatorname{odd}(M') = \sum_{i \text{ even}, 2\le i \le j-1} p_i + \sum_{i \text{ odd}, i \ge j+1} p_i$.

First player's total: $p_1 + \operatorname{odd}(M')$. $\operatorname{odd}(M) = p_1 + \sum_{i \text{ odd}, i \ge 3} p_i$.

Difference: $p_1 + \operatorname{odd}(M') - \operatorname{odd}(M) = \sum_{i \text{ even}, 2\le i\le j-1} p_i - \sum_{i\text{ odd}, 3 \le i \le j} p_i = (p_2 - p_3) + (p_4 - p_5) + \dots$.

Good.

Wait, but there's a subtlety: in the induction, the first player moves first on $M'$, so by induction he secures at least $\operatorname{odd}(M')$. Yes, since $|M'| = m - 2 < m$. Base cases $m \le 1$. Good.

Second player's guarantee: first player takes $p_j$. Second takes largest remaining $\ell$. Then on remainder, the second player of the original game is second player on $M''$. By induction secures at least $\operatorname{even}(M'')$. Total $\ell + \operatorname{even}(M'')$.

If $j = 1$: $\ell = p_2$, $M'' = \{p_3, \dots, p_m\}$; even-indexed: $p_4, p_6, \dots$. So $\ell + \operatorname{even}(M'') = p_2 + p_4 + \dots = \operatorname{even}(M)$. Good.

If $j \ge 2$: $\ell = p_1$, $M''$ sorted order $p_2, \dots, p_{j-1}, p_{j+1}, \dots, p_m$; position $i-1$ is $p_i$ for $i \le j-1$; position $i-2$ is $p_i$ for $i \ge j+1$. Even positions: $p_i$ with $i$ odd, $3 \le i \le j-1$; and $p_i$ with $i$ even, $i \ge j+1$.

For $j$ even: odd $i$ ranges $3,\dots,j-1$; even $i$ ranges $2, \dots, j$. Difference $= (p_1-p_2) + (p_3 - p_4) + \dots + (p_{j-1} - p_j) \ge 0$. Good.

For $j$ odd: odd $i$: $3, \dots, j-2$; even $i$: $2, \dots, j-1$. Difference $= (p_1 - p_2) + \dots + (p_{j-2} - p_{j-1}) \ge 0$. Good.
